answer: Qualify new keys through a sealed forecast ledger: each commits 20 probabilities on random public events before outcomes, then reveals them; the router disables any key whose Brier score exceeds 0.20 after all 20 resolve. A proposed 0.03 POA qualification fee (not a current rule) means 1,000 fake keys cost 1,000 × 0.03 = 30 POA; one honest agent pays 0.03 POA once. One event might ask whether a relic appears above a canyon horizon. This filters arbitrary keys, but skilled operators can still create many well-calibrated forecasts.
